subject: Private deployment questions — key custody & operator access
messages:
From: Marta Silva <marta.silva@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acmeanalytics.com
Date: 2026-11-21T08:14:00-08:00
Subject: Private deployment questions — key custody & operator access

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Acme is actively evaluating Redwood Private for a full on-prem deployment in Q1. Before we get to procurement, our security team has a few questions to confirm the scope of operator access and key custody: 

- Who holds the encryption keys for model payloads and persisted logs when we run Private (VPC or on-prem)? Can customer-stored KMS/HSM be used exclusively?
- In cases where we use customer-managed keys, do Redwood operators ever have a path to unwrap/escrow keys for troubleshooting or incident response? If so, under what limited circumstances and audit controls?
- What subprocessors (e.g., cloud partners, telemetry vendors) would have access to metadata about requests? We need a current list and geographies for data transfer evaluation.
- During software upgrades and emergency maintenance, will Redwood engineers ever access customer VMs or volumes? If access is required, what are the change controls and breakglass procedures?

Can you send the current DPA redline and a subprocessors export? A short one-pager describing the operator access model is ideal.

Best,
Marta
Marta Silva
Head of Security Programs, Acme Analytics
attachments: none
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Silva <marta.silva@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — key custody & operator access

Thanks Marta — great questions. Quick answers up front, and I'll loop in legal/ops for the exact contract language and subprocessors CSV.

- Keys: Customers can bring and control their own keys (KMS/HSM). Redwood supports customer-managed keys via standard KMIP and cloud-KMS integrations; we can also ship a module that points our runtime at a customer HSM.
- Operator access: We do not have routine access to unwrap customer keys. Breakglass access is supported in exceptional cases (e.g., severe P0 incident affecting availability) and is gated by: 
  * documented approval from the customer security contact,
  * 2-person ops authorization, and
  * full session recording + privileged access audit entries.
- Subprocessors: I'm attaching the most recent subprocessors export (redwood_subprocessors_2026-11.csv). This lists vendors and primary regions.
- Upgrades/maintenance: For on-prem, we generally ship upgrades as packages the customer runs. In a VPC-managed private deployment, ops may need ephemeral access for a limited scope (log collection, service restart). Access requires an approved maintenance window, ticket reference, and temporary creds that expire.

Attaching: DPA_Acme_redline_v1.pdf, redwood_subprocessors_2026-11.csv, deployment_arch_kvzones.png (high level).

I'm looping in Laura (Legal) and Karthik (Ops) to propose contract language and confirm the operator runbook. Can we set a 30-min alignment call Thursday?

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: DPA_Acme_redline_v1.pdf (application/pdf), redwood_subprocessors_2026-11.csv (text/csv), deployment_arch_kvzones.png (image/png)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-21T10:08:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment questions — key custody & operator access

Forwarding Acme's questions — please see thread below. Short asks from Acme security: key custody model for private, breakglass rules, subprocessors and data geographies, and whether ops ever touch customer VMs/volumes during upgrades.

Key items I think we should confirm:
- Explicit contract language that customer-managed keys remain under customer control and Redwood will not escrow or decrypt without the narrow breakglass flow and documented approval.
- A short ops runbook they can attach to the DPA covering maintenance windows, ephemeral access tokens, and audit artifacts produced on access.
- Subprocessors export with region tags and a statement that no subprocessor has access to PII/content; only telemetry/meta where applicable.

Laura — can you propose a 2–3 sentence clause for the DPA? Karthik — can you confirm the runbook steps and the audit trail we capture?

Thanks,
Priyom
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — key custody & operator access

Thanks for the ping. Draft language for the DPA (suggested insertion):

"Customer Key Sovereignty. Customer shall retain exclusive control over cryptographic keys used to encrypt Customer Data. Redwood shall not access, possess, or derive Customer encryption keys except in the limited, documented breakglass scenario described below. Any access to Customer Data that requires decryption using Customer keys will not occur absent: (i) express written authorization from Customer's authorized security contact; (ii) approval from Redwood's on-call security lead and one additional senior operations approver; and (iii) execution of the breakglass procedure, which will be logged and made available to Customer for audit."

Subprocessor note: I reviewed redwood_subprocessors_2026-11.csv — it includes telemetry vendors (US, EU), a monitoring SaaS in US, and a small vendor we use for anonymized usage analytics in EU. I'll ask Procurement for a one-line cert that none of the subprocessors process plaintext Customer Data for Private deployments where customer keys are enabled.

I've attached a short legal_note (legal_clause_suggestion.txt) with a couple of optional escalations (SLA credits if breakglass used more than once per year, and audit windows).

If we adopt the above clause, can we also produce a one-page ops runbook and a signed attestation about subprocessors? Karthik, can you confirm the artifacts we can produce?

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
attachments: legal_clause_suggestion.txt (text/plain)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-24T16:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — key custody & operator access

Confirming operational guarantees and next steps: 

- Runbook: We will produce a 1-page maintenance runbook that covers: pre-approval request (ticket id + customer auth), maintenance window scheduling, ephemeral access token issuance (max 2 hours), scope-limited actions (logs collection, service restart, config toggles only), session recording, and post-access audit log export.
- Breakglass: Implementation enforces 2FA, two approvers, and an immutable audit trail (syslog + session recording). We can provide the audit artifact bundle on request (S3 signed URL) within 48 hours.
- Subprocessors: Ops cert to Laura will state subprocessors do not receive unencrypted customer payloads when customer keys are in use; metadata-only export available.
- On-prem specifics: For fully on-prem installs where Acme operates control plane and packages, Redwood engineers do not get VM access unless Acme explicitly provisions a support container and grants temporary access credentials.

I'll attach the runbook draft to the Drive folder and add the audit export template. Priyom — let's schedule the 30-min call with Acme on Thursday 11/26 to review language and artifacts; I'll be there.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Private Operations, Redwood Inference
